overview: Under the Post-9/11 GI Bill, the Department of Veterans Affairs pays veterans' tuition and fees, and costs for flight training at public colleges can be very high. This bill sets a lifetime cap on how much the GI Bill will pay for tuition and fees for flight training at a public college, and for programs that a public college provides through a contract with an outside company, such as a private flight school. The cap is $119,684 for veterans who start such a program in the academic year beginning August 1, 2026, and rises each later year with the GI Bill's regular cost adjustment. The cap is reduced for veterans who qualify for only part of the full benefit, and by any GI Bill benefits a veteran already used before starting the program. As of September 8, 2026, it had been approved by a House committee and placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say a few flight programs have charged the GI Bill very large sums, often through outside contractors, and a cap protects taxpayer money and veterans' benefits from being used up on inflated costs.
against: Critics say flight training is expensive by nature, and a cap could force some veterans to pay out of pocket or drop plans for aviation careers.
